title: Rolapitant Injection
overview: Rolapitant injection is no longer available in the United States.

sections.Before receiving rolapitant injection,: tell your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to rolapitant; any other medications; soybean oil; legumes such as beans, peanuts, peas, or lentils; or any of the ingredients in rolapitant injection. Ask your pharmacist for a list of the ingredients.tell your doctor if you are taking thioridazine or pimozide (Orap). Your doctor will probably not want you to receive rolapitant injection if you are taking one or more of these medications.some medications should not be taken with rolapitant. Other medications may cause dosing changes or extra monitoring when taken with rolapitant. Make sure you have discussed any medications you are currently taking or plan to take before starting rolapitant with your doctor and pharmacist. Before starting, stopping, or changing any medications while taking rolapitant, please get the advice of your doctor or pharmacist.tell your doctor if you have or have ever had liver disease.tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while receiving rolapitant injection, call your doctor.
sections.Some side effects can be serious. If you: fever, chills, sore throat, or other signs of an infectionRolapitant injection may cause other side effects. Call your doctor if you have any unusual problems while taking this medication.If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may send a report to the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online (https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch) or by phone (1-800-332-1088).
